fields.options:
How a template works

Design the file in Excel or LibreOffice the way the client wants it, type placeholders into the cells, then upload it here. Use Download Starter Template to get a file with this doctype's fields already in place.

{{ doc.customer_name }}The field's value. If the cell holds only this, numbers and dates stay real numbers and dates, shown with the cell's Excel number format.
Invoice {{ doc.name }} for {{ doc.customer }}Text mixed with values.
{{ items.qty }}items is a child table, so this row repeats once per item. Every cell in a repeating row should use the same table.
{{ items|length }}Number of rows in a child table (in a normal cell).
{{ doc.items[0].item_code }}One specific child row.
{{ frappe.db.get_value("Customer", doc.customer, "tax_id") }}A value from another document, the same as in print formats.
{{ frappe.format(doc.grand_total, {"fieldtype": "Currency"}) }}A formatted value, as text.

Everything else in the file is kept: styles, merged cells, column widths, number formats, formulas, conditional formatting, dropdowns, images and print settings. When rows repeat, everything below moves down and formulas follow, so =SUM(D5:D5) under a repeating row 5 becomes =SUM(D5:D7) for three rows.

Shapes, text boxes, SmartArt, pivot tables and macros are not kept. You'll see a warning when you save if the file has them.

fields.label: XF Excel Format Help
fields.options:
Excel Format Help

Introduction

Excel Formats are generated using Python scripts in the backend. The doc object contains all the information about the document being exported. Additionally, you can access common utilities via the frappe module.

For styling and formatting, the openpyxl library is used, and relevant modules like Font, Alignment, Border, Side, PatternFill, and Image are pre-imported for use in your script.

References

  1. OpenPyXL Documentation
  2. Frappe Framework Documentation

Example Script

# Access pre-imported modules
wb = wb  # Workbook object
ws = wb.active  # Active worksheet
ws.title = doc.name  # Set sheet name as document name

# Set header styles
header_font = Font(bold=True)
alignment_center = Alignment(horizontal='center')
thin_border = Border(left=Side(style='thin'), right=Side(style='thin'), top=Side(style='thin'), bottom=Side(style='thin'))

# Add header row
headers = ['Item', 'Quantity', 'Rate', 'Amount']
for col_num, header in enumerate(headers, 1):
    cell = ws.cell(row=1, column=col_num, value=header)
    cell.font = header_font
    cell.alignment = alignment_center
    cell.border = thin_border

# Add data rows using doc object
row = 2
for item in doc.items:
    ws.cell(row=row, column=1, value=item.item_name)
    ws.cell(row=row, column=2, value=item.qty)
    ws.cell(row=row, column=3, value=item.rate)
    ws.cell(row=row, column=4, value=item.amount)
    row += 1

# Apply column width
for col in range(1, 5):
    ws.column_dimensions[get_column_letter(col)].width = 15

# Save Excel output (handled automatically by the export function)

Available Modules

  • doc: Document object that holds all form data
  • wb: Excel Workbook
  • ws: Worksheet (to be set manually)
  • Font: Style text fonts
  • Alignment: Align text in cells
  • Border: Set borders for cells
  • Side: Define border sides
  • PatternFill: Add background color
  • Image: Insert images
  • get_column_letter: Get Excel column letter

Common Functions

doc.get_formatted('[fieldname]', [parent_doc]) Get document value formatted as Date, Currency, etc. Pass parent doc for currency type fields.
frappe.db.get_value('[doctype]', '[name]', 'fieldname') Get value from another document.
frappe.utils.formatdate(date_string) Format date to a readable string.
frappe.get_doc('[doctype]', '[name]') Fetch a document for advanced data manipulation.
